predeclared_selection_rule.exact_quoted_text: the objective selection rule is: prefer (a) the pairwise reversal with the largest bootstrap-CI-excluding-zero effect size from §A, and (b) one representative *stable* ordering (largest tau, smallest CI) as a null-result control, so validation isn't confined to testing only positive findings.

reversal_case.selection_reasoning: Largest operationalized effect size (min(|margin_x|,|margin_y|), the binding constraint under the frozen practical-margin rule) among all 36 SUPPORTED_PRACTICAL_REVERSAL records for the PRIMARY metric.
reversal_case.tie_disclosure: Exactly tied (effect size 1.2816, bh_fdr_p 0.0) with the record {policy_a: slai_faithful, policy_b: vllm_faithful, condition_x: bailian_qwen::HIGH_PRESSURE, condition_y: burstgpt::HIGH_PRESSURE, load_region: HIGH_PRESSURE} -- both involve the same policy pair and the same burstgpt::HIGH_PRESSURE side; margin_y (the burstgpt-side margin) is the binding constraint in both and is effectively identical. Tie broken by the simplest available deterministic, non-subjective rule: lexicographic ordering of condition_x ('azure_llm_2024::HIGH_PRESSURE' < 'bailian_qwen::HIGH_PRESSURE'). The untied alternative is disclosed here rather than silently discarded; either choice tests the same scientific question (does the slai_faithful-vs-vllm_faithful ordering reverse between BurstGPT-like and non-BurstGPT-like traffic at HIGH_PRESSURE).

stable_control.selection_reasoning: Rule text order ('largest tau, smallest CI') interpreted as primary sort key = tau descending, secondary/tiebreak key = CI width ascending, applied over all 18 source-pair x region conditions for the PRIMARY metric. This condition has the single highest tau-b (1.0, a tie for the ceiling) among all 18 conditions.
stable_control.alternative_interpretation_disclosed: If 'smallest CI' were instead the primary sort key (CI-width first, tau second), azure_llm_2024::POST_KNEE vs bailian_qwen::POST_KNEE and azure_llm_2024::OVERLOAD vs bailian_qwen::OVERLOAD (both tau=0.9583, CI width=0.0417, narrower than the selected condition's CI width of 0.096) would be selected instead. Both alternative conditions are also Azure-2024 vs Bailian/Qwen pairs, consistent with the same source-pair identity as the selected control -- the choice of exact region does not change which source pair is used as the stable control, only which of the six regions.

vllm_faithful.note: Current vLLM release with chunked prefill disabled (--no-enable-chunked-prefill), per docs/REAL_SYSTEM_MECHANISM_INVENTORY.md. Adapter exists (real_llm/vllm_process.py) and was functionally smoke-tested this session.

slai_faithful.note: SLAI/RAD is a specific published SLO-aware scheduling algorithm (docs/POLICY_COMPARABILITY_AUDIT.md), not a vLLM-native scheduling mode -- unlike fifo (--scheduling-policy fcfs) or vllm_faithful (chunked-prefill flags), there is no existing --scheduling-policy value for it. vLLM 0.27.1 does expose a pluggable --scheduler-cls flag (confirmed via `vllm serve --help=SchedulerConfig`), so a custom scheduler class implementing the SLAI/RAD algorithm is a technically feasible, but NOT YET IMPLEMENTED, real-execution path. This was not identified as a gap in the earlier docs/REAL_SYSTEM_MECHANISM_INVENTORY.md pass because that pass only audited fifo/vllm_faithful/vllm_chunked_prefill_faithful/sarathi_faithful/weighted_fair_share/admission_control/apt_serve_faithful, not slai_faithful.

mechanism_mapping_status.blocker_for_execution: A custom vLLM --scheduler-cls implementation of the SLAI/RAD algorithm must be built and validated (unit-tested against the simulator's own slai_faithful policy for algorithmic fidelity) before the reversal case above can actually be executed on real hardware. This is a scoped, well-defined engineering task, not a design ambiguity.
